ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, six identical thick books are clamped between two identical vertical wooden boards, and the books remain stationary. At this time, the horizontal pressure applied to the boards on both sides is $F_{N}=40\mathrm{N}$. The mass of each book is $m=0.5\mathrm{kg}$, the gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathbf{s}^{2}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the boards and the books is 0.4. The maximum static friction force is equal to the sliding friction force.

1. What is the magnitude of the static friction force exerted by the left wooden board on the book?
2. What is the minimum coefficient of kinetic friction between the books?
3. What is the minimum vertical force required to pull out the second book from the left?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, six identical thick books are clamped between two identical vertical wooden boards, and the books remain stationary. At this time, the horizontal pressure applied to the boards on both sides is $F_{N}=40\mathrm{N}$. The mass of each book is $m=0.5\mathrm{kg}$, the gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathbf{s}^{2}$, and the coefficient of kinetic friction between the boards and the books is 0.4. The maximum static friction force is equal to the sliding friction force. 1. What is the magnitude of the static friction force exerted by the left wooden board on the book? 2. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, six identical vertical thick books can be seen clamped side by side between two identical vertical wooden boards on the left and right; on the left and right sides there are respectively horizontal inward pressures labeled F_N. The contact surfaces between the books and the wooden boards, and between book and book, are all vertical surfaces, therefore the directions of the frictional forces on these contact surfaces are all vertical directions. Reasoning: The weight of each book is mg=0.5×10=5 N, and the total weight of the six books is 30 N. The whole stack of books is at rest, and the only external vertical support that can be provided is the static friction force of the left and right wooden boards on the end books. Since the left and right structure and forces are symmetric, the upward static friction forces provided by the wooden boards on the two sides are equal, so each side is 30/2=15 N. The maximum friction force between the wooden board and the book is μF_N=0.4×40=16 N, greater than 15 N, therefore it is feasible. Analyze vertical equilibrium book by book from left to right. The 1st book is subjected to the upward friction force 15 N from the left wooden board and its own weight 5 N; in order to be balanced, the friction force between the 1st and 2nd books on the 1st book should be downward 10 N. By action and reaction, the 1st book acts upward 10 N on the 2nd book; the 2nd book's own weight is downward 5 N, therefore it also needs the 3rd book to act downward 5 N on the 2nd book. Continuing to the middle interface, the required friction force is 0, and the right half is symmetric. Therefore the maximum static friction force required between book and book is 10 N. The horizontal normal force between the books is transmitted as 40 N, so the minimum coefficient of friction is μ_min=10/40=0.25. If the 2nd book from the left is pulled out vertically upward, it has an upward tendency of motion relative to the adjacent books on the left and right, therefore the friction forces of the adjacent books on the left and right on it are both downward, and reach the limiting value μN=0.25×40=10 N. Adding the 2nd book's own weight 5 N, the required minimum upward pulling force is 10+10+5=25 N.
